description: Runs one polyphonic signal through sixteen insert channels, each channel adding to it, replacing it, crossfading, multiplying, comparing or limiting it.

params.text: Attenuates and inverts the main input before the inserts, -2 to +2.
Adds a fixed voltage to the main input before the inserts, -10V to +10V.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which follows the greater of the input's channel count and the furthest patched or normalled insert.
Scales that channel's insert input, and in Crossfade mode sets the blend between the main signal and the insert.
Offsets that channel: in most modes it shifts the final voltage; in Minimum, Maximum and Compare it shifts the insert side before the comparison, and alone sets the clamp level or threshold.

inputs.text: The polyphonic signal run through the sixteen insert channels.
The signal that channel's mode works on, taken through that channel's attenuverter and offset.

notes: each channel's mode button steps through Add, Insert, Crossfade, VCA bipolar, VCA unipolar, Minimum, Maximum and Compare; Compare puts out a clean 0V or 10V, and nothing else is clipped.
menu: Set all to — gives all sixteen insert channels the same mode at once.
Insert normalization — sets the insert inputs as independent, or lets a polyphonic insert fill the channels after it.
Main Input Polyphonic Wrap Mode — sets how the main input's channels are mapped when the output carries more channels than the input.
Multiple inserts break normalization — makes a later patched insert stop an earlier one's polyphonic normalling from reaching past it.
